headline: Highest risk is medium prompt-injection and data-leakage via AutoGen’s writable, networked workspace; Botpress adds no documented isolation or verification controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGen can read/write files, execute shell, and use stdin/stdout in a developer-defined shared workspace; Botpress has no documented isolation or provenance controls. That creates a plausible path for attacker-controlled content in shared files or messages to be treated as instructions. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes severity up.
conditions: IF AutoGen and Botpress share a filesystem or message channel, injected content can cross from one agent to the other.
IF Botpress consumes AutoGen-produced text as instructions without provenance checks, prompt injection is reachable.
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct workspaces.
Disable shared stdin/stdout bridging between agents.
Add provenance tags and reject untrusted instruction-like content.
Run AutoGen in DockerCommandLineCodeExecutor for isolation.
requires-engineering: add a sanitizer/allowlist for inter-agent messages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGen touches application data, reads/writes files, and has broad network egress; Botpress has no stated data-class limits or residency controls. If both see the same workspace, AutoGen can expose file contents to its model provider or downstream APIs. Botpress’s empty I/O surface makes the exact path less explicit, but the shared-data risk is still plausible.
conditions: IF both agents are configured on the same working directory, file contents can flow from one to the other.
IF AutoGen forwards workspace content to configured model providers, sensitive application data may leave the local environment.
mitigations: Use separate directories per agent.
Restrict AutoGen to non-sensitive sample data.
Turn off broad egress where possible.
Review model-provider logging and retention settings.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls on shared storage.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGen can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; Botpress can install packages. Even without explicit git overlap, both can mutate local state in the same environment, so concurrent writes or package changes can conflict. Because Botpress lacks concurrency details, the exact collision mode is uncertain and severity is raised to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents run in the same OS environment, package installs or file writes can race.
IF they share a mutable workspace, one agent can overwrite artifacts the other expects.
mitigations: Run agents in separate containers or venvs.
Freeze dependencies before concurrent runs.
Assign disjoint output directories.
Serialize package installation steps.
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGen is a multi-agent orchestration framework that can emit tool calls and code-execution outputs; Botpress is a customer-support agent that may act on conversational inputs. If Botpress treats AutoGen output as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect support actions or responses. No verification step is documented in either profile, so the safer medium rating is warranted.
conditions: IF Botpress consumes AutoGen output without a human or rule-based verification step, hallucinations can propagate.
IF AutoGen generates code or facts that Botpress reuses verbatim, downstream mistakes can multiply.
mitigations: Require human review before Botpress acts on AutoGen output.
Add schema validation for AutoGen outputs.
Use confidence thresholds before forwarding content.
Log and diff forwarded messages.
requires-engineering: implement a verification gate between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: AutoGen explicitly handles model-provider API keys and application data, while Botpress has no documented residency, retention, or certification constraints in the profile. There is no direct evidence of a specific regulatory mismatch, so only a low compliance risk is supportable. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from their combined handling of the same data class.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through both agents, retention and residency must be checked.
IF Botpress is deployed under stricter policy than AutoGen, policy mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Classify data before routing it to either agent.
Keep regulated data out of AutoGen workflows.
Document retention settings for both systems.
Review vendor terms and deployment region.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data residency and retention.
